_readme: Replay-ready payload for places_map_display_v0. Verify each place_id with places_search before use — ids change when a business moves or relists. See RECREATE-NATIVE-MAP.md.
title: Cleveland: The Odd & Overlooked
narrative: Nineteen stops grouped into three geographic clusters so you're not crossing the city twice. Day 1 is walkable downtown; Days 2 and 3 need a car or rideshare. Opening hours drive the order — a Friday-Saturday-Sunday trip threads every constraint; Monday-Wednesday misses several.

days.title: Downtown Core (mostly walkable)
days.narrative: Everything here is within about a mile, except the USS Cod which is a short walk over the Shoreway. Start early — the Terminal Tower deck is weekends only.

locations.name: Soldiers' & Sailors' Monument
locations.notes: Free inside. The famous tunnel labyrinth underneath is only opened one day a year — ask at the desk whether a tour is scheduled.

locations.name: Cleveland Public Library — Chess Collection
locations.notes: Main Building, 325 Superior Ave NE, third floor. World's largest chess collection. Bring photo ID — you're shown one item at a time. Closed Sundays.

locations.name: The Arcade
locations.notes: 1890 glass-roofed arcade modeled on Milan's Galleria. Rockefeller helped finance it. Grab lunch inside.

locations.name: Terminal Tower Observation Deck
locations.notes: Saturday/Sunday only, ~$5-6, tickets online in advance — no walk-ups. Two elevators: 32nd floor, then transfer to 42nd.

locations.name: Free Stamp (Willard Park)
locations.notes: Oldenburg & van Bruggen's giant rubber stamp. Two minutes to see, always open, worth the detour.

locations.name: USS Cod Submarine Memorial
locations.notes: Last fully intact WWII fleet sub. You enter by climbing down a vertical ladder — not accessible.

days.title: University Circle & the East Side
days.narrative: The museum cluster plus the cemetery. Note the Dittrick's very limited hours — it drives the whole day's schedule.

locations.name: Percy Skuy Collection, Dittrick Medical History Center
locations.notes: Only open Fri 10:30-4 and Sat 12-4. Free. 1,000+ contraceptive artifacts, from crocodile dung to Casanova's lemon halves.

locations.name: Cleveland Museum of Art
locations.notes: Free admission, one of the largest museums in the US. Enter from Wade Park for the best approach across the lagoon.

locations.name: Cleveland Museum of Natural History
locations.notes: Lucy, Balto, and an Apollo 12 moon rock on loan from NASA. Closed Mondays.

locations.name: Haserot Angel, Lake View Cemetery
locations.notes: Section 9, Lot 14 — grab a map at the gate. Closest landmark is the Hanna Mausoleum. Also here: Garfield's tomb, Wade Chapel, Alan Freed's jukebox headstone.

locations.name: Rockefeller Park Greenhouse
locations.notes: Closes at 4 — swap this earlier in the day if you want it. Free, 1905 city greenhouse. The Cultural Gardens run alongside.

locations.name: Quintana's Speakeasy
locations.notes: Back door of the barbershop, press the buzzer, say you're there to see a man about a horse. Then pull the right book off the shelf upstairs. Closed Mon & Sun.

days.title: West Side, Tremont & South
days.narrative: Market in the morning, oddities in the afternoon, sunset over Lake Erie. The market is closed Tuesdays and Thursdays — plan around it.

locations.name: West Side Market
locations.notes: Bring cash — most stalls don't take cards. Go in the morning for the meat and bakery halls. First hour of parking is free; park toward the back of the lot.

locations.name: Buckland Museum of Witchcraft & Magick
locations.notes: Gerald Gardner's artifacts, Sybil Leek's crystal ball, and a demon in a box. Small — allow an hour. Photos OK, no flash, no video.

locations.name: A Christmas Story House
locations.notes: House, museum and gift shop. Tours every 30 min. You can also book a night in Ralphie's bedroom.

locations.name: b.a. Sweetie Candy Company
locations.notes: A warehouse of candy. Went viral for a reason. There's a soda fountain inside too.

locations.name: Superelectric Pinball Parlor
locations.notes: Flat entry fee, unlimited play, beer at the bar. In Gordon Square, so pair it with the mural walk.

locations.name: The Sanctuary Museum
locations.notes: Hundreds of statues and stained glass rescued from closed Catholic parishes by a makeup artist. Only open Wed mornings and Sat afternoons — check first.

locations.name: Solstice Steps, Lakewood Park
locations.notes: Terraced stone steps down to Lake Erie. Best sunset spot in the region. Downtown skyline visible to the east.
